purpose: Registry of every retrieval mode present in the tree, recording whether it is actually scored by the benchmark harness, with file:line evidence. Built because benchmarks/results/latest.md scores four modes and never names the methods that are present but unmeasured.

repo.name: mem20
repo.baseline_subject: docs(ops): dispatch the 2026-10-27 workload roster — 22 agents, 1-hour round (#116)

diff_contract.ordering: modes[] is sorted by a fixed order: graph, hybrid, keyword, semantic, cross_encoder_rerank, then unscored modes by API surface, then MCP tools
diff_contract.promotion_rule: A mode may flip scored=false -> true only if it also gains measurement.n > 0 and a source_artifact that contains its per-query rows. A flip without measurement is a regression, not an improvement.
diff_contract.demotion_rule: scored=true -> false is a regression and must cite the commit that removed the harness branch.
diff_contract.compare_with: diff modes[].scored, then modes[].measurement.n. Any change in the first without a change in the second is a false promotion.

source_artifacts.role: derived view published by the reporting layer

source_artifacts.note: run() default modes tuple at line 248; _run_mode dispatch closes with raise ValueError(mode) at line 142, so any mode outside the four branches is a hard error, not a silent skip.
lines 61-63 wire only semantic and hybrid. Does not run keyword or graph.
Declares method status (working / working_but_score_degenerate / working_unverified_on_corpus) but carries no scored-vs-unscored field. This registry supplies that field.

notes: n=2. Two queries cannot support a quality claim; treat 1.000 as directional only.

modes.label: RRF fusion of dense vector + BM25 sparse, with optional cross-encoder rerank

evidence.note: def recall_hybrid(query, k=5, topic=None, tags=None, alpha=0.5)

notes: Adversarial hit_rate of 0.000 is assigned by the harness, not observed from retrieval; see adversarial_zero_is_structural.
Across all 13 published rows the table shows 0.692308 because the three structurally-zero adversarial rows are averaged in. Answerable-only hit rate is 0.900.
hybrid and keyword return identical quality on this corpus (both 0.900 answerable-only, 0.820 MRR), which is itself a finding: the vector half adds latency without adding recall here.

evidence.note: _run_mode branch: store.hybrid(q.text, k=k, alpha=0.0) - comment calls this the honest way to isolate the keyword half
method n=4 BM25 sparse, entry 'memory recall_hybrid (sparse half)', status working

One multi_hop query (m3) fails for keyword, hybrid and semantic alike, which points at the corpus or the evidence matcher rather than at any one retriever.

modes.label: Dense vector retrieval

evidence.note: _run_mode branch: store.semantic(q.text, k=k), returns the healthy flag
def recall_semantic(query, k=5, topic=None, tags=None, strict=False)
method n=3 dense vector, entry memory.recall_semantic, status working

notes: Semantic has the best answerable-only MRR of the three full-coverage modes (0.850 vs 0.820) at roughly one tenth of the hybrid latency.
It is the only mode whose result carries an index-drift diagnostic into the report (healthy flag).

modes.label: Cross-encoder reranking as a hybrid modifier

evidence.note: _rerank_comparison() measures hybrid with and without cross-encoder reranking
toggles engine.USE_CROSS_ENCODER and re-runs the hybrid arm twice
method n=6 cross-encoder rerank, status working_in_v2, with open defect CE-1 against memory.py

measurement.n_note: both arms run the full 13-query suite (5 direct + 5 multi_hop + 3 adversarial), so n is 26 observations across 2 arms

notes: This is the only experiment in the tree with a real control arm and a pre-registered contrast (on vs off), so it is the only one that supports a causal statement.
Reranking buys +0.10 direct MRR and costs 6.4x latency; it loses 0.16 multi-hop MRR. It is not a uniform improvement.
Scored as a variant of hybrid, never as a standalone mode, so no row attributes a hit rate to reranking alone.
modes.blocker: open defect CE-1: the memory.py recompute block emits no scores, so the in-engine rerank may be a no-op while retrieval_v2.rerank works

modes.label: Metadata-filter recall (topic / tags), no query text

evidence.note: raise ValueError(mode) - no branch for recall, so it cannot be scored even if named

notes: This is the metadata-filter method that METHOD_MANIFEST.json n=7 calls 'working'. It has never produced a number in any committed artifact.
It is the cheapest possible baseline and its absence means no scored mode has a pure-filter floor to beat.
modes.blocker: no _run_mode branch and no corpus query kind that is answerable by filter alone

modes.label: Bi-temporal point-in-time recall (valid-time + transaction-time)

evidence.note: def recall_at(as_of, **kw) - docstring 'what was true at as_of'

notes: This is the largest gap in the registry. mem20 sells retrieval trustworthiness as its differentiator, and bi-temporal correctness is the mechanism behind that claim, yet it has no measured row.
Closing it needs new query kinds (as-of anchors) in mem20benchmarkz/corpus.py and a new _run_mode branch, which is a harness change rather than a reporting change.
modes.blocker: corpus has no as-of query kind; needs corpus + harness change

modes.label: Entity listing (graph node enumeration by degree)
notes: Enumeration, not retrieval: it takes no query and has no expected-evidence target, so scoring it requires a different metric (coverage / precision of entity set), not hit rate.
Its only measured proxy is the trust block's graph_entities=38 / graph_edges=70, which is an inventory check, not a quality score.
modes.blocker: no metric shape in the harness for query-free enumeration

modes.label: Ledger tail read
notes: Raw append-only log read, not a ranked search. Correctly has no hit-rate row; it should be declared out of scope explicitly rather than left in a 'not yet measured' list that implies a debt.
It is load-bearing for audit claims, so it belongs under a durability test, not a retrieval benchmark.
modes.blocker: not a ranked retriever; out of scope for hit-rate scoring by construction

modes.label: Namespace-scoped shared recall with ACL check

evidence.note: handler _memory_shared_recall: ACL check then substring filter over namespace rows

notes: It has a distinct retrieval semantic - substring match over a namespace-filtered candidate set - so it is not merely recall() with a filter, and it cannot inherit recall's eventual number.
Its ACL denial path is the only measured thing about it (unit tests), and access control is not a retrieval-quality metric.
modes.blocker: not reachable from the benchmark harness; it lives behind the MCP server, which the harness does not drive

modes.label: Entity probe (all facts about one entity, trust-filtered)

evidence.note: registered as tool memory_probe, title 'Probe Entity'

notes: Entity-centric recall with a min_trust parameter. It is the natural place to measure precision under a trust threshold, and nothing measures it.
The trust threshold itself (default 0.3) is unvalidated: no artifact reports retrieval quality at any min_trust value.
modes.blocker: harness drives mem20api directly and never calls the MCP tool layer

modes.label: Structurally adjacent entity discovery
notes: Graph-adjacent but not graph(): it returns neighbours, not facts, so graph's 1.000 cannot be borrowed for it.
It is the mode most likely to be misrepresented as 'graph works', which is why it needs its own row.
modes.blocker: no expected-neighbour set in the corpus to score against

modes.label: Compositional reasoning across multiple entities

evidence.note: registered as tool memory_reason, 'Compositional reasoning across multiple entities'
present in the MCP tool namespace

notes: This is the only mode that claims multi-entity composition, which is exactly the multi_hop query kind the corpus already has - and multi_hop is the weakest measured class (0.800). The most interesting claim is therefore the one with no row.
Scoring it needs a judgement metric (answer correctness), not hit rate on a single evidence id.
modes.blocker: no correctness/judge metric in the harness

experiments.question: Does cross-encoder reranking improve hybrid ranking enough to justify its latency?
experiments.verdict: Conditional. Helps direct-query rank order, hurts multi-hop, costs 6.4x latency. Default-on is not justified by this data for multi-hop workloads.

experiments.verdict: Scaffold only. The harness README states no questions have been executed and the results table ships empty; no 5000QA number may be quoted.

experiments.question: R@k across mem20 retrieval methods on the isolated bench store.
experiments.verdict: Cannot be reproduced by anyone without the host's private bench store: it hard-codes a bench directory and a store path outside the repo, and it wires only semantic and hybrid, so it is a strict subset of the main harness. It has produced no committed artifact.

experiments.question: Can mem20benchmarkz run be re-executed from a clean clone?
experiments.verdict: No, not without the vector dependencies. With numpy and rank_bm25 present but no embedding stack, the freshly seeded store reports the vector index absent, and cli.cmd_run refuses to score an unhealthy store with exit code 2. Recomputing the published numbers therefore requires the embedding model the artifact records (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim) and the cross-encoder.

evidence.note: cmd_run returns 2 when the freshly seeded store is unhealthy

adversarial_zero_is_structural.claim: Every adversarial row in benchmarks/results/latest.md reads hit rate 0.000 for a structural reason, not because retrieval failed.
adversarial_zero_is_structural.mechanism: bench.py assigns hit=False and rank=None to every adversarial query unconditionally, before the result is used.

evidence.note: hit, rank = False, None - assigned unconditionally, never computed

adversarial_zero_is_structural.corroboration: In the per-query rows every one of the nine adversarial entries records n_results=5, i.e. retrieval did return five results each time. A retrieval failure could not produce five hits. The zero is the scorer, not the retriever.
consequence: The 0.000 is invariant to mode, corpus, index health and future code changes, so it cannot detect a regression.

The only adversarial signal that is actually measured is leak_rate (0.000 for all three modes over 3 queries each), which tests whether simulated content came back - a narrower property than abstention.
Averaging the three zeroed rows into a mode's headline hit rate depresses it mechanically: hybrid, keyword and semantic all publish 0.692308, while their answerable-only hit rate is 0.900.
The trust gate only fails on leak_rate, so an adversarial hit-rate regression could never break the build.
adversarial_zero_is_structural.what_to_measure_instead: Score adversarial queries on whether the top-k contains grounded evidence (abstention precision), which already has a per-query n_results field to build on.

gate_evidence.note: trust gate inspects leak_rate only, never adversarial hit_rate

open_gaps.gap: Adversarial hit rate is not measured anywhere; it is hard-coded to 0.000.
recall_at (bi-temporal) has no scored row, though it underpins the trustworthiness claim.
graph has n=2, which is below any defensible threshold for a quality claim.
Four MCP retrieval tools (memory_probe, memory_related, memory_shared_recall, memory_reason) are unreachable from the harness.
No gate fails when a present mode is presented as a scored one; nothing keeps a registry like this current.
open_gaps.evidence: cli.py:55-70 trust gate covers trust fields only

open_gaps.gap: Scale run (2000 facts) exists as code but has never been recorded.
